pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision
To inspire excellence in all.
Mission
Through our creative, dynamic learning environment we adapt to different needs, facilitate individuals’ aspirations and empower pupils to make a positive impact in their community.
Values
Our school values are the attitudes, skills and beliefs that we want to instil in our pupils so that they can succeed now and in the future.
Resilience
We build strength of character by encouraging everyone to rise to the challenge, take risks and grow from their experiences.
Respect
We ensure pupils recognise, learn from and value each other’s uniqueness within our diverse community.
Creativity
We foster inquisitive minds, that are curious to explore each opportunity and embrace transformational ideas.
Responsibility
We empower pupils to take responsibility for their actions and their surroundings in school, the local community and the wider world.
Integrity
We provide support through our secure and united community to give pupils the courage to be true to themselves and instigators of positive change.

Headteacher's Welcome
Adamsrill Primary School is a place where all staff are dedicated to providing a stimulating, exciting environment where everyone feels valued and safe.
Creativity and ideas can flourish, and children can maximise their progress.
By providing a varied and creative curriculum, which engages our children, and by promoting excellent behaviour, we aim to enthuse in all our children a desire to learn, as well as care and respect each other.
The Partnership between home and school is integral to your child’s success and we encourage parents to take an active part in their child’s learning. We see parents as playing a significant part in the education of their children, and greatly value their contribution to school life. Children thrive when they feel happy, safe and respected.
Whatever the needs of your child or special interests they have, we aim to ensure your child thrives at Adamsrill Primary School. We want the children here to have memorable experiences, build on what they know and can do and help them to become confident, life-long learners.
Adamsrill has a very successful Friend of Adamsrill Association who work together with the whole school community to raise funds for a wide variety of projects throughout the school; their support has enabled us to enhance the school’s provision in many areas.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for.
This school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
Dr Increase EsoeHeadteacher

Before School Wrap around Care
The school operates a wrap around care every morning, Monday to Friday, 7.45am to 08:50am.
This service is available to children in Reception through to Year 6.
About the Before School Wrap around Care
This facility is run by school staff, who are enthusiastic and dedicated about giving your child/children the best start to the morning.
Our aim is to ensure that children who use this facility are ready for the school day, by giving them a balanced breakfast and providing activities that will help their minds and bodies prepare for school. We want to strengthen relationships between school and home, building good communication and providing parents with peace of mind.
Registering
Places are only available to Adamsrill School pupils.
Priority will be given to children who require Monday to Friday places.
Remember that:
Costs are: £4 per child, per morning; £20 per week payable in advance via ParentPay.
PLEASE READ OUR FULL POLICY HERE
DEADLINE FOR SEPTEMBER START
If you are applying for a September start, the DEADLINE to submit your application is 30th JUNE every year. You might not get any response if you are applying after this date.

School Lunches
Our school lunches are provided by Olive Dining.
They pride themselves in their ability to provide nutritious healthy meals for pupils to enjoy and provide them with all the nutrients and energy to get them through their busy day. They offer a wide selection of choice to suit everybody’s taste to ensure we cater for the whole school.
Their menu offers a choice of fresh, healthy cooked food which meets the Government foodbased standards and has been nutritionally analysed to create balanced, healthy meals. Their menus retain the Food for Life Catering Mark and are freshly prepared using the finest, fresh, and local ingredients.
All meals are freshly prepared daily by a dedicated team using fresh ingredients. They operate menus on a 3 weekly cycle which includes main course, vegetarian course & a jacket potato or pasta option. All their menus meet and exceed all national nutritional standards.
For more information, please visit their website https://olivedining.co.uk/primary/

pageCache.text:
Meet our Governors
It is important that governors reflect the local community. People of all backgrounds, cultures, and races have a valuable contribution to make and should think about becoming a governor.
The Adamsrill School Governing Body is made up of parents, staff, and community members and we represent various walks of life and come from differing backgrounds.
The thing we all have in common is a passion that our children should have an outstanding education. Governors are elected/appointed for four years.
Our Governing Body provides strategic leadership and accountability across our school.
The Governing Body meets on a termly basis and has three core functions:
It is the responsibility of our Governing Body to:
overseeing the financial performance of the school
ensuring the school’s money is well spent
Ensure that financial procedures are sound
Participate in the appointment of staff
Shirley Hamilton
I have significant ties to the Sydenham/Forest Hill community, having lived in Forest Hill for the past 36+ years. Moreover, all three of my adult children attended Adamsrill; in fact two of my grandchildren have also attended the school; so I am particularly happy and proud to be able to sit on the schools Governing Board. I have an in depth knowledge of the demographics of the area as well as the potential needs of our community, given that I am also a Leader of one of the local faith groups. In this capacity, I have worked extensively and contributed positively to the community for almost 30 years.
Professionally, I have worked as a Curriculum Development Manager for an Adult Education College. I have a degree in Modern Foreign languages with International Studies, post graduate qualifications in Education and in Management. I qualified as a teacher in the post 16 sector, and worked in a variety of educational institutions for 20 years. Prior to that I had a managerial career in Lewisham Housing department and started my working life in the civil service.
As well as my duties managing multi-disciplinary teams in the adult education college, I was also a Teacher Educator. I am certain that my past and current experience will be of value to the school and I am willing to share my knowledge and skills as necessary.
Dillon Chiparimandu Vice Chair
Dillon Chiparimandu
Judy Evans
I became a parent governor at Adamsrill in 1990, when my two children attended the school and have been on the governing body ever since as a co-opted governor.
I have worked with school governors for many years as a Governance Officer and also co-ordinated training for governors. I am very ambitious for our pupils and support the Head teacher and staff with their hard work to ensure that each pupil reaches their full potential whilst at Adamsrill.
I am currently a joint Vice Chair of the Governing Board and a member of the Resources Committee and the Standards and Achievement Committee. I am also a link governor for Attendance and SEND.
Sue Bateson
I am Vice Chair of Governors at Adamsrill School and have a very long association with the school. I was born and brought up in South East London and was a pupil at Adamsrill (with my brother and cousins and I remember playing on the grassy field where the new building now is). When both my children were pupils at school in the 1990s, I became active in the PTA. I was first elected as a parent governor and later became a co-opted governor.
I was elected six years ago and have seen the school through many changes and three OFSTED inspections during that time. I am the designated governor for safeguarding and lead for governors on Health and Safety matters.
I still live locally and have spent my working career in the housing field. I am currently a civil servant.
Lennox Hamilton Vice Chair of Resources
Lennox Hamilton
I have several years experience of school governance and governance in the community sector. I have been a Local Authority appointed governor and have served as the chair of the Premise Committee. My previous and current work experience have stood me in good stead as a Governor.
As a senior Project Manager and Consultant, I regularly work with, and on behalf of, school staff; including Senior Leaders, Teaching and Support Staff. Moreover, I have experience of over 17 years in Education Construction Project and Facilities Management, and prior to that 15 years in Housing Estates and Property Management, at senior level.
I am educated to Degree Level: A Bachelor of Humanities Degree, University of London. I am a qualified Prince 2 Project Management Practitioner; holder of P405 Asbestos Management Qualification; Level 4 qualification in Management of Health and Safety; trained Psychodynamic Counsellor; qualified Reflexologist (ITEC Level 3 Diploma).
I have a wealth of Leadership experience; including as Senior Pastor of a local church, and an ordained Bishop in good standing. I have served as adviser to the former Mayor of Lewisham, and active Community Champion on Race Equality issues.
My connection to Adamsrill has spanned over three decades, my three grown up children attended the school as part of the nursery until they left at the end of year 6. I have also had two of my four grandchildren educated at the school. My years as a governor initially started in the 1990s, I have a strong commitment to the local and school community.
Stuart Dayman
I've been a parent at Adamsrill since 2011 and currently have a daughter in year 3. Previously a professional musician, I'm working closely with the music department as a link governor. At present I'm working for Transport for London as an operational development manager in air quality schemes. I believe in the importance of having a great education experience and I want our children at Adamsrill to be given the best opportunities to learn and develop in all aspects of school life.
Vanessa Croan
I wish to serve as a Parent Governor to support the school to achieve and stretch its academic objectives while also bringing its community together to celebrate and grow understanding of diversity, equality and inclusion.The last two years have been particularly challenging for many of us; a global pandemic, a growing climate crisis, racial injustice, a widening socio-economic gap, and, most recently, conflict that feels very near to home.I want children to feel that school is a safe place to learn and ask questions to grow their knowledge and also challenge and reflect on issues important to our society, equipping them both academically and emotionally as they enter high school and grow into young adults.As a Parent Governor, I will support the governing body to be a link between the school and community and hold the school to account for its responsibilities to our children and community. I am personable, both open and fair-minded, and enthusiastic about making a difference at Adamsrill.
Ewan Mitchell Chair of Resources
Ewan Mitchell
I have worked as a data scientist and team leader in the financial services for ten years. This includes five years at a credit ratings company where he took ACCA accountancy training and built statistical models based on companies' financial reports to assess their financial health. Prior to that I spent seven years working in secondary schools as a mathematics teacher and head of department. I taught math at all levels including A level and Oxbridge entrance and was a member of the academic policy committee. I have a PGCE, a distinction in post graduate statistics from Sheffield University, a DPhil (doctorate) in Astrophysics from Oxford University and a Masters in Natural Sciences from Cambridge University.
Michael Noonan
I became a Parent Governor at the start of 2023. I currently have one child at the school and anotherwho is due to start reception this year. My wife & I have made Sydenham our home and very much enjoybeing part of the local community.After graduating with a degree in Economics I commenced a career in banking, currently working for alarge international bank. I've undertaking numerous roles and I now look after a portfolio of businessclients. This involves relationship building, data analysis, problem solving, managing budgets, projectmanagement and communicating with multiple stakeholders. I'd like to use the skills developedthroughout my varied career for the benefit of the school and local community.As part of the school governors, I want to help create and ensure a positive experience for all pupils atAdamsrill. I'm passionate about all pupils reaching their potential and developing the foundationbuilding blocks during their primary education years to set them up for success in their future life. Icurrently sit on the Standards and Achievement committee.
Emilia Gentle
I'm a counsellor and therapist working in private practice since 2019. My background is in theatre and film and since qualifying as a therapist in 2017, I've been working to combine two of my passions - providing mental health support to those who need it, and working with the Arts sector. Alongside my private practice, I work for an organisation that provides therapy to those working in the Arts. My knowledge and experience in this field can be helpful when working with this group of people.
I have a degree in English and a degree in Counselling and psychotherapy. I lived in Canada for a few years where I worked for an EAP (Employee Assistance Programme). It was here that my interest inmental health and offering mental health support, began. I'm originally from South London and attended South London state schools throughout my childhood.
It's partly because of this that I feel passionately about our local schools and investing time and effort in to supporting the children and the staff to ensure everyone receives equal opportunities and education. I have two wonderful daughters at Adamsrill. We're part of a rich community in Sydenham and at Adamsrill, and I look forward to becoming even more a part of this community through becoming a parent governor.
Diana Valcheva
I am delighted to have recently joined the Governing Board at Adamsrill Primary School as the Local Authority Governor. I bring over 30 years of experience in early years, primary, and system leadership. I currently serve as the Headteacher of Kate Greenaway Nursery School and Children's Centre, a highly regarded maintained nursery school in Islington known for its inclusive ethos, nurturing environment, and innovative early education. Alongside my headship, I also work as an Ofsted Inspector and hold the NPQEL, NPQH, and Level 7 Executive Coaching and Mentoring qualifications. I am passionate about giving every child the best possible start in life and supporting the people who make that possible. I live in Lewisham and care deeply about my local community. I look forward to working with the team at Adamsrill to contribute to its ongoing success and to help all children flourish and become the best version of themselves.
Sonia Miguez Jorge
I have 23 years of experience in education and have worked across all phases, including EYFS, as well asin a range of leadership roles (with the exception of headship). Alongside my teaching degree, I havecompleted the NPQSL and NPQH, and I am currently completing the final module of my NPQSENCO. I havealso recently undertaken Safer Recruitment training.I keep up to date with curriculum and assessment developments and have led numerous successfulschool-wide initiatives over the years. I am currently responsible for Curriculum, Assessment, RE, RSE andPSHE in a Catholic school, and I previously served as Maths Lead for several years.I have been a Deputy Headteacher for the past five years and work closely with the governing body—attending all meetings, preparing agendas, and producing documentation for the Curriculum & StandardsCommittee and the Catholic Life Committee. I also coordinate Governor Week, organising visits, meetings,and engagement across the school.A significant part of my leadership experience includes inspection preparation and leadership. Isuccessfully led our Section 48 Inspection, which resulted in an Outstanding judgement, and I played apivotal role in our most recent Section 5 Ofsted inspection, contributing to its highly successful outcome.In addition, I oversee the Pupil Premium Strategy and Sports Premium Report, ensuring compliance andimpact. I also represent the school in local authority review meetings and work closely with our SchoolImprovement Partner to disseminate key actions and priorities.I work collaboratively with the School Business Manager to ensure full website compliance, regularlyreviewing statutory requirements and keeping curriculum and policy information up to date.

Adamsrill is two-form primary school We take in up to 60 children in our reception year group, 30 children in each class.

Nursery Admission
Adamsrill Nursery offers places to children aged 3 & 4 years
Most children, after attending the Nursery, are offered places in one of our two Reception classes. There are 60 places in the Reception classes and a small number of children who have not been through our Nursery are admitted.
It should be noted that an offer of a Nursery place does not guarantee an offer of a place in a Reception class. You must apply again for admission into the Reception classes. Places are allocated by Lewisham Education Admissions Team, you can find more information on the Lewisham website.
Our Reception and Nursery September intake is staggered, and all children benefit from a home visit before starting.
The Nursery can offer part-time places to 26 children in the morning and 26 children in the afternoon. This will be 16 full-time places and 18 part-time places (depending on demand, this can be reviewed).
Full-time sessions: 30 hours
Part-time sessions: 15 hours
Morning session: 9:00am – 12:00pm
Afternoon session: 12:30pm – 3:25pm
All sessions are offered across five days per week during term time only. Please note that these hours must be taken in this format and cannot be combined or used flexibly across fewer days.
Nursery Funding and Charges
At Adamsrill Primary School, there are no additional charges for your child to attend our Nursery if they are eligible for either the 15-hour or 30-hour funded entitlement and, where applicable, you provide a valid 30-hour childcare code.
Children attending a 30-hour place are required to bring a packed lunch each day. All nursery children also receive fresh fruit and milk daily at no additional cost.
If your child is not eligible for the 30-hour funded entitlement but you would like them to attend a 30-hour nursery place, you may purchase the additional hours that are not covered by government funding. Charges for these additional hours will be set up at the start of each term through our ParentPay system.
The current charge for additional nursery hours is £6.75 per hour.
For a full breakdown of costs, funding arrangements, and payment information, please contact the school office, who will be happy to assist.
Only Nursery admissions are managed by the school.

"We are Nut-Free school. We set out all measures to reduce the risk to those children and adults who may suffer an anaphylactic reaction if exposed to nuts to which they are sensitive. We aim to protect children who have allergies to nuts yet also help them, as they grow up, to take responsibility as to what foods they can eat and to be aware of where they may be put at risk. We do not allow nuts or nut products in school lunch boxes.
The following items should not be brought into school: Packs of nuts, Peanut butter sandwiches, fruit and cereal bars that contain nuts, Chocolate bars or sweets that contain nuts, Sesame seed rolls (children allergic to nuts may also have a severe reaction to sesame), Cakes made with nuts.

My School Fund Scheme
We’re pleased to announce that Adamsrill Primary School is part of the My School Fund initiative. This innovative scheme allows our parents/staff and school to be able to boost their finances by receiving 2% cash-back and it is COMPLETELY FREE to sign up.
Parents, guardians, and carers can sign up to the scheme for free and start earning cashback on the things they buy in participating retail stores, including Sainsbury’s and Argos. As you spend you’ll receive 2% cashback in the form of eGift vouchers that can be redeemed in participating stores. By adding a credit/debit card and linking your spending to our school on the My School Fund website, the school also earns 1% cashback on your spending.
Add that all up across our school’s network of families and together we can all make a big difference!
Visit myschoolfund.org to register for free, link to Adamsrill Primary School, and add your credit/debit card. From there, everything you spend in participating stores will go towards helping boost your school's budget, plus your own! Sign up today at myschoolfund.org.
